citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
citations.narrative:
During Inspection, APHIS Officials were not able to inspect the pharmacy as the pharmacist was on vacation and the
attending veterinarian (AV), clinical veterinarians, and pharmacist technician did not have a key for the pharmacy. The
pharmacist will not be back until later in the week. In the mean time, the attending veterinarian and clinical veterinarians
do not have access to drugs during regular hours or during an emergency. The AV not having a key to the pharmacy,
undermines the AV's role and authority in ensuring provision of adequate veterinary care of animals under their care.
Each research facility shall assure that the attending veterinarian has appropriate authority to ensure the provision of
adequate veterinary care and to oversee the adequacy of other aspects of animal care and use.
Correct from today forward.

During inspection of the Animal House APHIS officials observed multiple floor areas in need of repair in the indoor
housing facility in the kennel rooms holding multiple dogs. The primary enclosures of the indoor housing facility holding
dogs have damaged epoxy floor and wall areas where porous concrete is in contact with the animals. The floor was
previously sealed with epoxy, but areas have peeled off and have exposed the porous concrete. The areas exposed
range from approximately 3 inches to 15 inches long.
Surfaces that are permeable to moisture cannot be properly cleaned and/or sanitized, which can negatively affect animal
health. The floor must be impervious to moisture to allow proper cleaning and sanitation. The floors and walls of indoor
housing facilities, and any other surfaces in contact with the animals, must be impervious to moisture.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with Attending Veterinarian.
Additional Inspectors:
Lemnique Wafer, Assistant Director n
